newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Family demands proof slain Arab sold land to Jews.
newsitem.headline: Family demands proof slain Arab sold land to Jews.

text.p: Relatives of a Palestinian who was killed last week amid accusations he sold land to Jews rejected the charge on Monday and said they would ignore a ban on his burial in a Moslem cemetary unless proof was produced.
The PLO-appointed Mufti of Jerusalem, the city's top Moslem cleric, said 70-year-old Farid Bashiti could not be buried in a Moslem graveyard.
"None of the rumours going around about my father are true. My father was an honest Palestinian and Moslem," said his son, Muhammed Bashiti.
The dead man's cousin Aasem Bashiti told reporters: "We are giving the people and the authority a three-day period to present proof that he sold land to Israel."
"Otherwise, if they do not, we will pray on his body in three days at al-Aqsa," the relative said, referring to the Jerusalem mosque that is Islam's third holiest site.
The Palestinian Authority said last week it would apply the death sentence to Palestinians who sold land to Israelis.

Bashiti was found dead in PLO-ruled Ramallah in the West Bank on Friday. Security sources said he was discovered bound and with signs of a blow to the head by a sharp object. Israel was investigating the death after Palestinian security forces handed over the body.
Jerusalem Mufti Ikrima Sabri said the Bashiti family had informed him of the three-day deadline for proof of the charges against Farid. But his position had not changed.

"We did not accept, there was no agreement between us. We will not intervene. This is the affair of the family but our position has not changed. Anyone who sells land to Israelis will not be buried in a Moslem graveyard and they should not pray at his body," he said.
